S20-F1-Q1.skill: Prove that the elimination step keeps the same solutions
S20-F1-Q1.prompt:
System A: x + y = 9 and x - y = 3.
System B: x + y = 9 and 2x = 12 (its second equation is the sum of the two equations of A).

S35-F2-Q1.skill: Explain the SAS, ASA, and SSS criteria with rigid motions
S35-F2-Q1.prompt:
Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, angle A = angle D, and AC = DF (SAS).
Explain the rigid motions that map triangle ABC onto triangle DEF, and why C must land on F.
S35-F2-Q1.correct_answer: A rigid motion maps A to D, B to E, and C to F, so the triangles are congruent.
S35-F2-Q1.required_method: A complete argument: translate A to D; rotate so ray AB lies along ray DE, and B lands on E because AB = DE; if C is on the other side of DE from F, reflect across DE. Since angle A = angle D, ray AC lies along ray DF, and since AC = DF, C lands on F. Any equivalent order is accepted.

S35-F2-Q2.skill: Explain the SAS, ASA, and SSS criteria with rigid motions
S35-F2-Q2.prompt:

S35-F2-Q2.correct_answer: C lands on F, so the triangles are congruent.
S35-F2-Q2.required_method: Because angle A = angle D, the image of ray AC lies along ray DF; because angle B = angle E, the image of ray BC lies along ray EF. C is on both rays, and the two rays meet at only one point, F.

S35-F2-Q3.skill: Explain the SAS, ASA, and SSS criteria with rigid motions

S35-F2-Q3.correct_answer: C is at distance AC from D and BC from E. On that side of DE, only one point (F) is at those two distances (the two circles meet there once), so C lands on F.

S64-F1-Q1.skill: Prove that lines are parallel from congruent angles
S64-F1-Q1.prompt:
Lines m and n are cut by transversal t, and a pair of alternate interior angles is congruent.
Explain why m and n must be parallel. (Suppose they meet at a point P, and look at the triangle formed with t.)
S64-F1-Q1.required_method: A complete argument: if m and n met at P, they would form a triangle with t. One of the congruent angles would be an exterior angle of that triangle and the other a remote interior angle. But an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so it is greater than either one. That is a contradiction, so m and n do not meet: they are parallel.

S64-F1-Q4.skill: Prove that lines are parallel from congruent angles

S43-M-Q4.skill: Use the angle-angle criterion to show that triangles are similar

S43-M-Q4.correct_answer: The triangles share angle A, and angle ADE = angle ABC (corresponding angles, because DE ∥ BC). So they are similar by AA.

S43-F1-Q1.skill: Establish the angle-angle criterion with similarity transformations
S43-F1-Q1.prompt:
Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E.

S43-F1-Q1.correct_answer: A dilation that makes AB the same length as DE, followed by rigid motions that move the image onto DEF; the equal angles make the third vertices match.

S43-F1-Q2.skill: Establish the angle-angle criterion with similarity transformations
S43-F1-Q2.prompt:
Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E.
Explain why a similarity transformation maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF.
S43-F1-Q2.correct_answer: Dilate ABC by the scale factor DE ÷ AB, so the image of AB has the same length as DE. Rigid motions then move that image onto DE (A onto D, B onto E), with the third vertex on the same side as F. Because angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E, the image's other two sides lie along rays DF and EF, and two rays meet in only one point, so the third vertex lands on F. (The third angles are then equal too.)
S43-F1-Q2.grading_note: Full credit needs the dilation, the rigid motions, and why the third vertex must land on F.

S44-M-Q1.skill: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean theorem and its converse
S44-M-Q1.prompt:

S45-F1-Q1.skill: Prove the converse of the Pythagorean theorem with congruent triangles
S45-F1-Q1.prompt:
Triangle ABC has sides BC = a, AC = b, and AB = c, with a² + b² = c².
Prove that angle C is a right angle. (Build a right triangle with legs a and b.)
S45-F1-Q1.required_method: A complete proof: build right triangle DEF with legs EF = a and DF = b and its right angle at F. By the Pythagorean theorem, DE² = a² + b² = c², so DE = c. Then triangles ABC and DEF have all three pairs of sides equal, so they are congruent (SSS), and angle C = angle F = 90°.

S45-F1-Q2.prompt: In that proof, which congruence criterion is used, and why does it apply?

The level drops about 0.3 foot each day.

S57-M-Q1.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables
S57-M-Q1.prompt:
60 students were asked whether they have a curfew and whether they have chores. 36 have a curfew. 24 of the students with a curfew have chores. 8 of the students without a curfew have chores.
Complete the two-way table.
S57-M-Q1.correct_answer: Curfew: 24 chores, 12 no chores, 36 total. No curfew: 8 chores, 16 no chores, 24 total. Totals: 32 chores, 28 no chores, 60 in all.

S57-M-Q3.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables

90 people were asked whether they exercise daily and whether they eat breakfast. 40 exercise daily. 30 of the people who exercise daily eat breakfast. 50 of the 90 people eat breakfast.
Complete the two-way table.
S57-M-Q3.correct_answer: Exercises: 30 breakfast, 10 no breakfast, 40 total. Does not: 20 breakfast, 30 no breakfast, 50 total. Totals: 50 breakfast, 40 no breakfast, 90 in all.

S57-M-Q4.prompt:
Ten students answered two questions: "Do you have a pet?" and "Do you have a sibling?" Their answers (pet, sibling) are:
yes–yes, yes–no, no–no, yes–yes, no–yes, yes–yes, no–no, no–yes, yes–no, no–no
Complete the two-way table.
S57-M-Q4.correct_answer: Pet: 3 sibling, 2 no sibling, 5 total. No pet: 2 sibling, 3 no sibling, 5 total. Totals: 5 sibling, 5 no sibling, 10 in all.

S57-M-Q5.skill: Construct a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables
S57-M-Q5.prompt: A completed two-way table for 60 students has exactly two rows, Curfew and No curfew, and every student is in one of them. Its row totals can be 36 and 20.
S57-M-Q5.grading_note: Every student is in exactly one of the two rows, so the row totals must add to 60.
